passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The Companies’ businesses are influenced by many factors that are difficult to predict, that may be beyond their control and that involve uncertainties that may materially affect actual operating results, cash flows and financial condition. See “Risk Factors” in Item 1A. Critical Accounting Estimates The Companies’ financial statements reflect the application of certain critical accounting estimates, which conform to accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. The Companies’ critical accounting estimates include assumptions applied to accounting for: pensions and other postretirement benefits, contingencies, derivative instruments, allowance for uncollectible accounts receivable, asset retirement obligations and income taxes. Also, see “Summary of Significant Accounting Policies and Other Matters” in Note A to the financial statements in Item 8. Accounting for Pensions and Other Postretirement Benefits The Utilities provide pensions and other postretirement benefits to substantially all of their employees and retirees. Con Edison Transmission also provides such benefits to transferred employees who previously worked for the Utilities. The Companies account for these benefits in accordance with the accounting rules for retirement benefits. In addition, the Utilities apply the accounting rules for regulated operations to account for the regulatory treatment of these obligations (which, as described in Note B to the financial statements in Item 8, reconciles the amounts reflected in rates for the costs of the benefit to the costs actually incurred). In applying these accounting policies, the Companies have made critical estimates related to actuarial assumptions, including assumptions of expected returns on plan assets, discount rates, health care cost trends and future compensation. See Notes A, E and F to the financial statements in Item 8 for information about the Companies’ pension and other postretirement benefits, the actuarial assumptions, actual performance, amortization of investment and other actuarial gains and losses and calculated plan costs for 2025, 2024 and 2023. The discount rate for determining the present value of future period benefit payments is determined using a model to match the durations of Aa rated (by either Moody’s or S&P) corporate bonds with the projected stream of benefit payments. In determining the health care cost trend rate, the Companies review actual recent cost trends and projected future trends. The cost of pension and other postretirement benefits in future periods will depend on actual returns on plan assets, assumptions for future periods, contributions and benefit experience. Con Edison’s and CECONY’s current estimates for 2026 are decreases, compared with 2025, in their pension and other postretirement benefits credits of $256 million and $243 million, respectively, largely driven by decreases in the discount rates used to determine plan liabilities. See Notes E and F to the financial statements in Item 8. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow covers the dividend more than four times over, and buybacks are nil, so shareholder distributions absorb only a modest share of internally generated funds and leave room for the regulated capital programme.

Gross leverage improved year on year and now sits below the utilities sector median on the same definition, with net leverage similarly below the peer median, indicating deleveraging relative to a regulated-utility peer group.

key_risks.text: Interest coverage is thin at roughly two and a third times operating income and sits below the sector median, so a modest earnings setback or refinancing at higher coupons would compress headroom against the next risk band.

The filing flags pension and other postretirement obligations as a critical estimate, with expected declines in benefit credits driven by lower discount rates; adverse actuarial experience or rate treatment would pressure earnings and cash flow.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Cash flow to debt improved year on year and exceeds the sector median, and the ratio clears the next risk-band boundary with comfortable headroom, supporting the view that internal cash generation services the borrowing base.

Maturities are light near term, with only a small slice due within twelve months and the bulk falling after year five, so refinancing risk is modest; the current ratio is above one and above the sector median, though it slipped year on year.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is aggressive, driven by leverage and cash-flow tiers, yet leverage sits below the sector median and improved year on year, so the profile reflects a capital-intensive regulated utility rather than idiosyncratic weakness.

Operating margin is stable year on year but well below the sector median, and capital expenditure is not disclosed, so free cash flow and its coverage of distributions remain unknown; this gap is material to the cash-flow view and warrants filing-level review.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流覆蓋股息超過四倍，且並無回購，因此股東分派僅佔內部產生資金的一小部分，為受監管資本計劃留有空間。
總槓桿按年改善，現時低於按同一定義計算的公用事業行業中位數，淨槓桿亦同樣低於同業中位數，顯示相對受監管公用事業同業組別正在去槓桿。

key_risks.text: 利息覆蓋率偏薄，約為營運收入的兩倍三分之一，並低於行業中位數，因此輕微的盈利挫折或按較高票息再融資，將會壓縮相對下一個風險區間的緩衝空間。
申報文件將退休金及其他退休後責任列為關鍵估計，並預期福利抵免因折現率下降而減少；不利的精算經驗或費率處理將對盈利及現金流構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 現金流對債務比率按年改善並高於行業中位數，且該比率以充裕緩衝越過下一個風險區間界線，支持內部現金產生足以償付借款基礎的觀點。
近期到期債務較少，僅一小部分於十二個月內到期，大部分於第五年之後到期，因此再融資風險溫和；流動比率高於一且高於行業中位數，儘管按年有所下滑。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為激進，由槓桿及現金流層級所驅動，然而槓桿低於行業中位數並按年改善，因此該狀況反映的是資本密集的受監管公用事業，而非個別性弱點。
營運利潤率按年穩定但遠低於行業中位數，且資本開支未予披露，因此自由現金流及其對分派的覆蓋情況仍然未知；此缺口對現金流觀點屬重大，值得進行申報文件層面的審閱。
